title: Friday Football Frenzy: Sept. 25, 2026 Scores, Highlights & Game Recaps – WLOS Sports roundup
body:
The region’s high‑school football scene ignited under the Friday night lights on September 25, delivering a cascade of upsets, record‑breaking performances, and playoff‑shaping outcomes that will reverberate through the rest of the season. From the high‑octane showdown in Asheville to tightly contested battles across western North Carolina, week six of the Friday Football Frenzy saw five teams secure their first victories of the year while two perennial powerhouses cemented their dominance, setting the stage for a dramatic run‑in to the postseason.

In the marquee matchup at Asheville High School, the Bulldogs edged out the defending district champions, the Hendersonville Hurricanes, 28‑24 in a game that featured a last‑minute drive orchestrated by senior quarterback Mason “Mace” Reynolds. Reynolds, who threw for 312 yards and three touchdowns, capped his effort with a 12‑yard touchdown pass to wide receiver Jordan Lee as time expired, snapping the Hurricanes’ three‑game winning streak. The Bulldogs, who entered the night 0‑4, rallied behind a stout defensive front that forced two critical turnovers in the fourth quarter, including a fumble recovery that set up the game‑winning score. Coach Luis Martinez praised his team’s resilience, noting that “the boys showed they belong here; they fought for every inch and earned this win.”

A few miles east, the Marion County Mountaineers delivered a dominant 42‑7 victory over the Rutherford Rams, showcasing a balanced attack that highlighted the emergence of sophomore running back Tyrell Jackson. Jackson rushed for 178 yards on 21 carries and added two touchdowns, becoming the first underclassman to break the 150‑yard mark for Marion County this season. The Mountaineers’ defense, anchored by senior linebacker Caleb Ortiz, limited Rutherford to a single field goal and forced three sacks, reinforcing the team’s reputation as a two‑way threat. The win propelled Marion County to a 3‑2 record, keeping them in contention for the district’s top seed.

In the western foothills, the Cherokee High School Warriors upset the top‑ranked Asheville‑Buncombe 31‑27 in a game that will be remembered for its dramatic fourth‑quarter comeback. Trailing 24‑10 at halftime, the Warriors’ offense, led by junior quarterback Eli Carter, ignited a 21‑point surge that included a 68‑yard run by running back Malik Torres and a 45‑yard interception return for a touchdown by safety Darius Hall. The victory not only snapped Asheville‑Buncombe’s unbeaten run but also vaulted Cherokee into a tie for second place in the district, intensifying the race for the coveted playoff berth.

Meanwhile, the Catawba Valley Cavaliers continued their march toward the district crown with a 35‑14 triumph over the Hickory Ridge Hawks. Quarterback Riley Anderson threw for 285 yards and four touchdowns, while the Cavaliers’ special teams unit contributed a 92‑yard kickoff return for a score, underscoring the team’s depth across all phases of the game. Anderson’s poise in the pocket, combined with a disciplined defensive line that recorded eight tackles for loss, highlighted why Catawba Valley remains a favorite to clinch the district title.

The final highlight of the night came from the East Rutherford Eagles, who posted a gritty 21‑20 win over the Gaston County Panthers after a blocked field goal in the final seconds preserved their lead. Freshman kicker Tyler Brooks, who had missed two earlier attempts, redeemed himself by nailing the decisive extra point, showcasing the mental toughness that has become a hallmark of the Eagles’ program. Their victory marks a crucial turning point, as the Eagles now sit at 4‑1 and are poised to challenge the district’s traditional powerhouses in the weeks ahead.

As the Friday Football Frenzy rolls into its seventh week, coaches and players alike will be scrutinizing the emerging trends: a surge in dual‑threat quarterbacks, heightened defensive aggression, and a noticeable shift toward faster, more versatile skill positions. The early-season volatility suggests that the district championships will be decided not only by talent but by depth, adaptability, and the ability to execute under pressure. Fans can expect the next slate of games to deliver further surprises, as teams that have found momentum seek to solidify their standings while those on the brink of a slump look to regroup. With playoff implications mounting, every Friday night will prove to be a pivotal chapter in a season that promises to be as unpredictable as it is exhilarating.
